{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABYsLGCg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhCRBns", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 15, "title": "Handle reserved GDMA I/O port 0x43 without aborting 16-bit accesses", "body": "## Problem

The Color/Crystal General DMA implementation introduced in #13 supports register ports `0x40–0x42` and `0x44–0x48` but **rejects port `0x43`** as an unsupported I/O access:

```
Unsupported output port 0x0043.
```

The V30MZ CPU implements a 16-bit `OUT` / `IN` operation by accessing two consecutive 8-bit ports. A valid `OUT DX, AX` starting at `DX=0x0042` therefore reaches `0x42` (low byte) followed by **`0x43`** (high byte). Currently the latter triggers an execution fault, although `0x43` is the unused upper byte of the DMA source segment register rather than a separate implemented DMA feature.

The GDMA unit test `byte_register_masks_readback_model_and_mode_gates` in `crates/ws-core/src/gdma_tests.rs` currently **explicitly asserts** that `0x43` read/write should fail, so the implementation and tests must be corrected together.

This is a **generic I/O compatibility issue**, not a request for any particular ROM or a reason to make all unknown ports silently succeed. Do not include commercial ROM dumps or proprietary firmware in tests.

## Expected outcome

On **WonderSwan Color and SwanCrystal**, 8-bit and 16-bit I/O involving the reserved GDMA port `0x43` no longer aborts emulation:

- An 8-bit write to `0x43` succeeds but has **no effect** on the 20-bit GDMA source address, transfer state, or neighboring registers.
- A read from `0x43` returns a deterministic `0x00` in the implemented model, while documenting that its exact hardware electrical readback is not confirmed by physical-device tests.
- A 16-bit `OUT DX, AX` or `IN AX, DX` with `DX=0x0042` completes normally. Only the **low nibble of the value written to `0x42`** contributes to the DMA source address's high four bits; the high byte corresponding to `0x43` is ignored/read as zero.
- The existing GDMA engine, its masked register behavior, and the **mono model gating** remain intact. Other genuinely unsupported ports retain their explicit errors.

## Context and independent evidence

Inspect the current source before changing it:

- [`crates/ws-core/src/bus.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/crates/ws-core/src/bus.rs): `input` and `output` handle `0x40..=0x42 | 0x44..=0x48` only for Color/Crystal; `0x43` takes the unsupported-port path.
- [`crates/ws-core/src/cpu.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/crates/ws-core/src/cpu.rs): wide `IN` and `OUT` access `port` and `port.wrapping_add(1)`; no ROM tracing is required to demonstrate this general execution path.
- [`crates/ws-core/src/gdma_tests.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/crates/ws-core/src/gdma_tests.rs): existing test expects port `0x43` to fail.
- [WSdev General DMA documentation](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/DMA): source address is 20 bits occupying three meaningful bytes `0x40–0x42`, and destination/length/control start at `0x44`.
- Independent reference behavior from **reading source for comparison only** (do **not** copy/port emulator code):
  - [MAME `wswan.cpp`](https://github.com/mamedev/mame/blob/master/src/mame/bandai/wswan.cpp): treats the `0x42/0x43` pair as a 16-bit source segment register and masks the resulting value to `0x000f`, discarding the high byte.
  - [ares `cpu/io.cpp`](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/blob/master/ares/ws/cpu/io.cpp): handles meaningful `0x40–0x42` DMA registers and ignores unmatched mapped writes rather than stopping.
  - [Beetle/Mednafen `wswan-memory.c`](https://github.com/libretro/beetle-wswan-libretro/blob/master/mednafen/wswan/wswan-memory.c): does not mutate DMA registers on `0x43` writes, and its generic unmatched-port read returns zero.
- Historical references contain uncertain descriptions for `0x43`; the proposed read-zero behavior is an **evidence-based emulation policy**, not a claim of confirmed electrical behavior on original hardware.

Follow the repository [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md) and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md): English contributions, minimal coherent scope, executable pre-merge acceptance, and honest validation.

## Implementation guidance

1. Add a narrowly scoped Color/Crystal `0x43` match in the Rust bus I/O read and write paths. Return zero on read; ignore data on write; preserve existing generic I/O time accounting rather than inventing DMA work. No separate `0x43` stored state is necessary.
2. Keep this behavior **model-gated**: original WonderSwan mono must not gain color-only GDMA functionality.
3. Update the existing GDMA test that expects `0x43` to error, while leaving `0x49` and `0x4A`/Sound DMA genuinely unsupported. Ensure writes with nonzero byte values are ignored, not just writes of zero.
4. Add CPU-level tests using self-authored machine code for `OUT DX, AX` and `IN AX, DX` at port `0x0042`, asserting the resulting registers, source address, execution continuation and absence of execution fault. Exercise both Color and Crystal, and separate 8-bit read/write. Verify that the neighboring GDMA source register and real transfer behavior still work.
5. Update the [hardware support document](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/hardware-subset.md#general-dma-semantics) to specify reserved high-byte semantics and remaining uncertainty. Avoid unrelated changes to DMA scheduling/CPU instruction execution or to the web UI.

### Explicitly out of scope

Broad unknown-port fallback, implementation of Sound DMA or other unimplemented I/O features, changes to unrelated CPU instruction families, commercial-ROM compatibility promises, ROM-specific conditional logic, and new runtime tracing/debug panels.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] 8-bit I/O to `0x43` is ignored on write and returns `0x00` on read for Color/Crystal; tests verify several **nonzero** written values do not alter any neighboring GDMA state.
- [ ] On Color and Crystal, native CPU tests execute `OUT DX, AX` and `IN AX, DX` with `DX=0x0042` without error and confirm the effective source segment is only four bits. Verify CPU instruction progression is not halted by the reserved byte.
- [ ] Tests establish the **original mono model retains its documented restrictions**, and `0x49` and unimplemented Sound DMA ports still produce explicit unsupported-port errors. No blanket permissive handling is introduced.
- [ ] Existing GDMA, CPU, cartridge, graphics/audio, and original self-authored ROM tests still pass; the GDMA transfer and clock behaviors from #13 do not regress.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `npm run build:wasm`, and `npm run build` pass using actual repository tooling; report checks performed, failures, and skipped checks honestly.
- [ ] Hardware documentation accurately states the implemented reserved-port handling and clearly distinguishes emulation policy from physically verified hardware behavior. No proprietary ROM/BIOS, copied emulator core, or unrelated framework is added.

## Optional validation

Compare the reserved-port readback on a physical WonderSwan Color or SwanCrystal, if available; physical hardware access is not required for approval. A locally built self-authored homebrew test ROM may supplement native CPU tests.

## Required post-merge verification

1. **Pending:** Verify the existing GitHub Pages workflow succeeds for the resulting `main` merge commit and record the Actions run URL and status.
2. **Pending:** If a freely redistributable homebrew I/O test cartridge is provided, optionally exercise it on the deployed page and record the observed outcome. Do not require a proprietary cartridge for publication verification.

Live deployment checks must not be treated as completed before merge.
